summary.en: Mina, Arafat and Muzdalifah with millions of pilgrims. Agree on your camp and meeting points before each move.

detail.en: Learn your camp number, its gate and a nearby landmark. Save the camp as a meeting point in the app before you leave it. Roads and camps in Mina look very alike.

name.en: A numbered gate of the Grand Mosque

detail.en: Every gate has a number, for example King Abdulaziz Gate 1 and King Fahd Gate 79. Agree on one gate number with your group.
If your group uses the metro, agree on the station you will meet at. There are three stations each in Arafat, Muzdalifah and Mina.
A fixed place everyone can reach on their own if the group is split for hours.

dos.en: Keep your camp number and group leader details with you on paper as well as on your phone.
Set a meeting point in the app before every move: Mina, Arafat, Muzdalifah, Jamarat.
Drink water often and rest in the shade in the hottest hours.
Keep your phone charged and switch Mesh Radar to Balanced mode on long days.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.
Move with the flow and work your way diagonally toward the edge.

donts.en: Don't leave your group to take a shortcut through the crowd.
Don't go to the Jamarat outside your group's scheduled time.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.
Don't stand against walls, fences or barricades when a crowd is dense.

detail.en: Pilgrims enter ihram for Hajj and most spend the day and night in Mina.
Move from Mina to Arafat and stay until sunset, then go to Muzdalifah for the night.
Stone Jamrat al-Aqabah, offer the sacrifice, shave or trim, and perform Tawaf al-Ifadah.

title.en: 11 to 13 Dhu al-Hijjah, Days of Tashreeq

detail.en: Stay in Mina and stone all three Jamarat each day.

meaning.en: I am looking for my family

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Camp number, hotel name and group leader phone saved in the emergency card.
Meeting points added for the camp, a mosque gate and the hotel.
Power bank, charging cable and a printed copy of the lost-child card for children.
Comfortable sandals, umbrella for shade, refillable water bottle.
Practice an SOS together and run one regroup drill before you travel.

summary.en: Umrah at the Grand Mosque, busiest in Ramadan. Use gate numbers to meet up and keep your permits ready.

name.en: A numbered gate of the Grand Mosque

detail.en: Every gate has its own number, for example King Abdulaziz Gate 1, Safa Gate 11, Fath Gate 45, Umrah Gate 62, King Fahd Gate 79 and King Abdullah Gate 100. The Ministry advises agreeing on a door number before you start.
A fixed place everyone can reach on their own.
Gates can close when full (the gate panel turns red), so also agree on a spot outside it.

dos.en: Book your Umrah and prayer permits in the Nusuk app before you go.
Agree on a gate number before every visit to the mosque.
Check the gate panels: green means entry is open, red means that gate is full.
Keep elders and children close in the mataf and on the way out after prayers.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.

donts.en: Don't wait for a lost person inside the mataf. Go to your agreed gate.
Don't block doors or stairways after prayers.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.

detail.en: The Ministry calendar runs the season from 14 Dhu al-Hijjah 1447 to 30 Shawwal 1448 (about 31 May 2026 to 7 April 2027).
The mosque is busiest in the last ten nights. Plan meeting points before each night prayer.

meaning.en: I am looking for my family

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Nusuk permits booked for Umrah and for the Rawdah if you plan to visit.
Hotel name and group leader phone saved in the emergency card.
A gate number and a hotel added as meeting points.
Power bank and charging cable.

summary.en: The walk from Najaf to Karbala, about 80 km over 2 to 3 days. Use the numbered poles to meet up.

name.en: A pole number on the route

detail.en: The route is marked by 1452 numbered poles about 50 m apart. Agree on a pole number for each day.
Guides list centres at poles 72, 335, 602 and 1103, and at the shrine of al-Abbas. Check they are still there this year.

name.en: The shrine of al-Abbas in Karbala

detail.en: Pole 1452 is where the route enters Karbala near the shrine.
Save the place you sleep as a meeting point before you leave it in the morning.

dos.en: Start after the dawn prayer and walk until sunset, with rests in the heat of the day.
Stay with the main crowd on the main road rather than side roads.
Agree on a pole number to meet at every few hours.
Look after your feet: spare socks, plasters and good shoes.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.

donts.en: Don't walk alone at night.
Don't let children walk ahead of the group in dense crowds near Karbala.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.
Don't stand against walls, fences or barricades when a crowd is dense.

detail.en: Najaf to Karbala is about 80 km and usually takes 2 to 3 days on foot.
20 Safar. The date depends on the moon, so it can move by a day.

meaning.en: I am looking for my family

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Children carry a printed lost-child card.
Comfortable shoes, spare socks, plasters, a light bag.
Power bank: you may not find charging points for hours.
Set the app to Balanced mode for the walk.

summary.en: The Tablighi Ijtema near Lahore, held in two phases. Plan your way in and out, and meet at fixed places.

detail.en: Save your camp or block as a meeting point as soon as you arrive.
Traffic police set up numbered parking stands. Note yours and save it.
The station has extra staff and a medical camp during the Ijtema.

dos.en: Plan your trip home before the closing dua: roads in Raiwind close and traffic runs one way toward Lahore.
Park only in the official parking stands.
Rescue 1122 has medical teams at the Ijtema. Note where the nearest one is.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.

donts.en: Don't park outside the stands or on roads kept clear for emergency vehicles.
Don't try to leave with the whole crowd right after the dua if you can wait.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.

detail.en: The Ijtema is held in two phases about a week apart, usually in November. Each ends with a collective dua.
In recent years extra trains have stopped at Raiwind, and in 2025 the Punjab government ran an electric bus from Lahore railway station and the airport. Check this year's arrangements.

meaning.en: I am looking for my family

phrasebook.phrase: میں اپنے گھر والوں کو ڈھونڈ رہا ہوں
phrasebook.transliteration: main apne ghar walon ko dhoond raha hoon

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Camp or block and parking stand saved as meeting points.
Power bank and charging cable.
A plan for the trip home after the closing dua.

summary.en: Majlis gatherings and processions in the first ten days of Muharram. Know the route and keep children close.

detail.en: The place your family gathers for majlis. Save it as a meeting point.
Pick a fixed point on the procession route before it starts, away from the narrowest streets.

name.en: The end point of the procession

detail.en: For example Hussainian Iranian Imambargah in Karachi, Masjid-e-Ilahi in Hyderabad, or the Karbala site by Dhanmondi Lake in Dhaka.

dos.en: Check this year's procession route and timings with local police notices.
Keep children and elders on the edge of the procession, not in the middle.
Drink water often. Sabeel stalls are common but carry your own too.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.
Move with the flow and work your way diagonally toward the edge.

donts.en: Don't go into the narrowest lanes of the route when the crowd is densest.
Don't stand right at the end of the route in Karbala during the Tuwairij run: a crush there in 2019 killed at least 31 people.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.
Don't stand against walls, fences or barricades when a crowd is dense.

detail.en: Majlis gatherings each evening, with processions on 9 and 10 Muharram in many cities.
Pakistan, India and Bangladesh often observe Ashura a day after Saudi Arabia, as in 2026.

meaning.en: I am looking for my family

phrasebook.phrase: میں اپنے گھر والوں کو ڈھونڈ رہا ہوں
phrasebook.transliteration: main apne ghar walon ko dhoond raha hoon

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Children carry a printed lost-child card.
Meeting points saved for your imambargah and one point on the route.
Power bank and charging cable.

summary.en: Bathing days at Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik-Trimbakeshwar and Ujjain. Know your sector, ghat and the lost and found centres.

label.en: Mauni Amavasya, the biggest Magh Mela bathing day

detail.en: Mela areas are split into numbered or colour coded sectors, and ghats are numbered. Save yours as soon as you arrive.
At Maha Kumbh 2025 the mela authority ran lost and found centres across the mela area where people without a phone could call family. Note the nearest one.
Pick one end of a named bridge, not the middle.
The main bathing places at the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha.

dos.en: Go to bathe early on the big days, or on a quieter day if you can.
Agree on a ghat and a time to meet after bathing.
Keep elders and children on the side of the ghat, away from the steps where people push down.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.
Move with the flow and work your way diagonally toward the edge.
If you fall, get up fast. If you cannot, curl up on your side and cover your head with your arms.

donts.en: Don't stop on bridges, steps or narrow approach roads.
Don't go into deep water: stay within the ropes and barricades.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.
Don't stand against walls, fences or barricades when a crowd is dense.

detail.en: 14 Jan, 6 Feb, 11 Feb, 20 Feb, 6 Mar, 8 Mar, 7 Apr, 14 Apr, 15 Apr and 20 Apr. Amrit Snans are 6 Mar, 8 Mar and 14 Apr.
Where the Ganga and Yamuna meet, about 7 km from Civil Lines. Boats leave from the ghat near the fort.

meaning.en: Where is the lost and found centre?

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Children carry a printed lost-child card.
Sector, ghat and camp saved as meeting points.
Dry clothes in a plastic bag, a towel and a power bank.
Practice an SOS together and run one regroup drill before you travel.

summary.en: Pandal hopping in Kolkata, across West Bengal and in Bangladesh. Pick meeting points at each pandal and at the metro.

label.en: Durga Puja 2026, West Bengal (Shashthi to Bijoya Dashami)

detail.en: Agree on a spot outside before you go into every pandal, since the way out is often different from the way in.
Kolkata Metro runs late into the night on Saptami, Ashtami and Navami. Pick one station and one exit.
Save where you parked as a meeting point.

dos.en: Use the Kolkata Police Puja Guide Map to plan your route.
Go to the busiest pandals early in the day or after midnight.
Hold children's hands in queues and at pandal exits.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.

donts.en: Don't follow the crowd into a pandal without agreeing where to meet outside.
Don't stand close to the river edge during immersion processions.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.

detail.en: The busiest nights for pandal hopping.
Immersion processions. In Dhaka the main one goes from Dhakeshwari National Temple to Wiseghat on the Buriganga.

meaning.en: Where is the police help booth?

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Children carry a printed lost-child card.
A pandal list for the night, shared with the group.
Power bank and charging cable.

summary.en: Three chariots pulled about 3 km along Bada Danda to the Gundicha Temple. Meet away from the chariot ropes.

name.en: A side street off Bada Danda

detail.en: Pick a named side street, not the Grand Road itself, which fills edge to edge.
Where the chariots stop, about 3 km from the main temple.
A fixed place everyone can reach on their own.

dos.en: Watch from a side street or a building with permission rather than the middle of the road.
Agree on a meeting point before the chariots start moving.
Drink water often: it is hot and humid in late June and July.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.
Move with the flow and work your way diagonally toward the edge.
If you fall, get up fast. If you cannot, curl up on your side and cover your head with your arms.

donts.en: Don't get between the crowd and the chariot wheels or ropes.
Don't take small children into the crowd near the chariots.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.
Don't stand against walls, fences or barricades when a crowd is dense.

detail.en: Balabhadra (Taladhwaja, 14 wheels) goes first, then Subhadra (Darpadalana, 12 wheels), then Jagannath (Nandighosa, 16 wheels).
The deities stay at the Gundicha Temple for seven days.
The return journey on the ninth day, followed by Suna Besha, when the deities wear gold on their chariots.

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Children carry a printed lost-child card.
A side street and your hotel saved as meeting points.
Water bottle, cap and power bank.

summary.en: Big matches mean crowded gates before and after play. Meet by block or enclosure and leave together.

detail.en: Stadiums sell seats by block letter (Eden Gardens) or named enclosure (Gaddafi Stadium). Save yours as a meeting point.
Pick a gate on the side you will leave from, and a fixed spot a little away from it.

name.en: Your car, bus or rickshaw stand

detail.en: Save it before you go in.

dos.en: Arrive early and know your gate and block before you queue.
After the match, wait for the first rush to clear before you leave.
Venues can change late: check the official schedule on match day.
Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.
Move with the flow and work your way diagonally toward the edge.

donts.en: Don't join a crowd outside the gates for victory celebrations: a crush at Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru killed 11 people in June 2025.
Don't go to the stadium without a ticket hoping to get in.
Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.
Don't stand against walls, fences or barricades when a crowd is dense.

detail.en: The PCB confirmed 18 March to 2 May 2027 for PSL 12. Venues were not announced at the time of writing.
The 2027 schedule had not been announced at the time of writing.

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card.
Block or enclosure and an outside gate saved as meeting points.
Power bank and charging cable.

summary.en: Loud, dark and packed. Pick a meeting point you can find without a phone signal and keep away from barriers.

detail.en: A sound desk, a numbered tower or a food stall sign, not a moving crowd spot.
Pick the exit nearest your meeting point when you arrive.
A second spot outside, in case you are split up when everyone leaves.

dos.en: Find the exits and a second way out as soon as you arrive.
In a dense crowd, keep your hands up near your chest to protect your breathing.
Move with the flow and work your way diagonally toward the edge.
Agree on a time to check in by the app, for example after every third song.
If you fall, get up fast. If you cannot, curl up on your side and cover your head with your arms.

donts.en: Don't push against the flow of a crowd, and don't stop or sit down in it.
Don't stand against walls, fences or barricades when a crowd is dense.
Don't rush for shelter all at once if it starts to rain: a crush on steps at Cochin University in 2023 started this way.

checklist.en: Every group member has the app and has joined the group.
A landmark and an outside spot saved as meeting points.
Power bank and charging cable.
Ear protection for children.

summary.en: Treks in Nepal, Gilgit-Baltistan and the Indian Himalaya. Set check-in timers and keep the group within reach.

detail.en: Save it as a meeting point every morning before you set off.
The leader can add checkpoints with deadlines in the app.

name.en: A Himalayan Rescue Association aid post

detail.en: On the Everest route at Pheriche and on the Annapurna route at Manang, staffed in spring and autumn.

dos.en: Set a check-in timer before every day on the trail.
Keep the slowest walker in the middle of the group, not at the back.
Check permit rules before you go: in parts of Nepal you need a licensed guide and a TIMS card.
Register your trek with the tourism department in Gilgit-Baltistan.
Climb slowly and rest when anyone has a headache, nausea or dizziness at altitude.

donts.en: Don't leave the trail to take a shortcut, especially in fog or snow.
Don't split the group without agreeing where and when you will meet again.
Don't keep climbing with symptoms of altitude sickness.

detail.en: The Nepal Tourism Board lists spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) as the best months for the Annapurna area. Other areas differ.

checklist.en: Every group member has the app, has joined the group and has filled in their emergency card, including blood group.
Permits, TIMS card or registration done for your route.
Check-in plan with checkpoints and deadlines set by the leader.
Power bank, headlamp, warm layers, water purification.
Set the app to Balanced mode; use Ultra-saver when battery is low.

summary.en: When the network and power fail, the mesh keeps your family in touch. Agree on where to go before you need it.

detail.en: A school, mosque, temple or upper floor everyone in the family knows.
Add it as a meeting point when local authorities announce it.

name.en: A relative's home outside the flood area

detail.en: Somewhere to regroup if you are separated for days.

dos.en: Agree on a family meeting point on high ground before the monsoon.
Keep phones and power banks charged when a warning is issued, and switch the app to Ultra-saver if the power is out.
Use a stick to check for open manholes and drains when you must walk in water.
Switch off electricity at home before water comes in.
Follow warnings from your national meteorological department.

donts.en: Don't walk through moving water: even a shallow current can knock an adult down.
Don't drive into flooded roads: about half a metre of water can carry a car away.
Don't go near power lines in a flood.

detail.en: India June to September (northeast monsoon in the south October to December), Pakistan July to September, Nepal normally mid June to early October, Bangladesh flood season April to October. Real onset moves by weeks.
On 23 January 2023 Pakistan's national grid failed nationwide; mobile towers were affected and many areas were dark for over 12 hours. The mesh works without towers or power.

checklist.en: Every family member has the app, has joined the family group and has filled in their emergency card.
A family meeting point on high ground saved in the app.
Charged power banks, torch, drinking water, medicines and copies of documents in a waterproof bag.
If you use Family Circle, turn it on for the family group before the season.
